title: Expert onboarding: from a new account to a working practice
summary: The wizard is calm and honest, but it is an admin form: it opens with a tax number, never asks who the expert is, and never shows her the profile she is building. It also sits inside a dashboard whose every link sends her back to the form, and a new account that came to offer care lands on a member Space with no visible way in. The change that matters most is to rebuild setup as one focused, full-screen journey in profile-first order (about you, how you see members, first service, licence, payouts, invoices) with a live profile preview, then open the dashboard with a checklist.
strengths: The finish step says exactly what happens next in plain words: 'When you finish, we check your licence with your Ordem. Members can book you once it's verified.' Keep this honesty (06-setup-step-5).

The licence intro is good trust copy: 'Eleva lists regulated health professionals only. We check these details with your professional body before members can find you.' The 'Why we ask' disclosures are the right instinct (06-setup-step-2).
The Online / In person / Phone cards are large, tappable and have a sensible default; they work well on mobile (06-setup-step-1.mobile).
The tax number is optional ('You can add it later') and Portugal is preselected and locked in the country list, so nothing blocks a Portuguese expert early.
Stripe onboarding is embedded in the page, so the expert never leaves Eleva. The engineering choice is right; only the words around it are weak.
The cream, teal and Lora system holds together on every step, and the desktop step rail is easy to read.
A hook already exists: the avatar menu offers a shortcut to create an expert workspace when the account has none (packages/dashboard/src/account-menu-model.ts). It only needs to be visible.

findings.title: A new account that came to offer care lands on a member Space with no way in
findings.detail: Every sign-up returns to /dashboard and opens the member Space: 'Welcome, Marta', two empty session lists and two 'Find an expert' buttons. Nothing on the page, the sidebar or the mobile header says a health professional can offer care here. The only route is one line inside the avatar menu, or knowing the /account/workspaces URL. A physiotherapist who arrived from /become-expert has just been told she is a member and will reasonably conclude she signed up in the wrong place. This is the gap between 'account created' and 'I am an expert here', and it loses experts before the wizard is ever seen. The repo already holds the fork pattern: _context/mobbin/Apps/web/onboarding/Time2book Web Onboarding/ (Client vs Business) and PoC O6 Path Fork.
findings.recommendation: Carry intent through sign-up: links from /become-expert and the expert sign-up variant (see AUTH-01) add intent=expert, and after verification that account skips the member Space and opens practice setup. For everyone else, add a quiet, dismissible card on the member Space home ('Are you a health professional? Offer care on Eleva') and a permanent 'Offer care on Eleva' link in the sidebar footer and the mobile menu. The card opens a short benefits sheet (three lines and 'Get started'), not the workspace type picker.

findings.title: The wizard sits inside a dashboard the expert is not allowed to use
findings.detail: The setup form is drawn inside the full practice chrome: Today, Calendar, Services, Members, Public profile, Schedule, Finance and eight more links, with 'Today' highlighted. Until setup is finished every one of them returns to the wizard. The page promises a product and then refuses it twelve times. It also splits attention: a 255 px sidebar, a title column and the form compete on desktop, and on mobile the sidebar toggle opens a menu that goes nowhere. Airbnb, Fresha and Etsy all remove navigation during setup and give it back afterwards.
findings.recommendation: Run the required steps as a focused full-screen flow: logo, 'Save and exit', 'Questions?', one question area, a segmented progress bar and Back / Continue. No sidebar. When the required steps are sent, open the real dashboard with a setup checklist on Today (ONB-12). If the team prefers to let experts look around first, do the opposite consistently: unlock the dashboard read-only and put the checklist on Today. Either works; the current mix of both does not.

findings.title: Setup opens with a tax number and never asks who the expert is
findings.detail: The first question a new expert meets is 'Tax number (NIF)'. The five steps are tax and meeting mode, country and licence, payouts, invoicing, finish. Not one asks her profession, speciality, photo, a line about how she helps, or her first service and price: the things members will see and the reason she joined. Those are pushed to 'Meanwhile you can' cards at the very end. Admin comes first and motivation never arrives, which is the reverse of the Airbnb order the founder wants (tell us about your place, make it stand out, then finish and publish). Etsy places 'How you'll get paid' and billing after naming and stocking the shop for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: Reorder to profile first, money last: 1) About you (profession, speciality, photo; name prefilled). 2) How you see members (online, in person, phone; where you are based; languages). 3) Your first service (name, length, price). 4) Your licence. 5) Get paid (Stripe). 6) Invoices (the NIF belongs here, next to the thing it is used for). 7) Review and send. Steps 1 to 3 build something she can see; 4 to 6 are easier to accept once there is a profile worth protecting.

findings.title: 'Where you practise' packs five goals and about twelve controls into one step
findings.detail: One step asks for practice country, every country she may work in (checkboxes, a second dropdown and an 'Add EU countries' button), languages (checkboxes and another dropdown), professional body, licence number, ERS registration number and a 'Worldwide remote (non-clinical only)' option, with two collapsed 'Why we ask' panels in between. On mobile it is about 1,840 px tall with the button at the very bottom. This is the opposite of one goal per step, and the hardest fields (the licence numbers) arrive buried mid-scroll. 'Clinical modes still follow the countries above' is internal language. The repo's Fresha flow (_context/mobbin/Apps/web/setting up/Fresha Web Setting up an account/) shows the same kind of information asked one question per screen.
findings.recommendation: Split it: 'Where are you based?' with languages on one screen (two answers, both prefilled from locale), and the licence on its own screen (ONB-11). Move 'other countries you may work in' and 'worldwide remote' out of first-run setup into practice settings, reachable from the checklist as 'See members in other countries'. Most Portuguese experts will never need them on day one.

findings.title: The expert never sees her public profile taking shape
findings.detail: On desktop the left third of every step repeats the same static block: 'Set up your practice', 'A few short steps and you're ready to welcome members', a progress card and the step list. It never changes and shows nothing of the result. There is no preview, no 'this is how members will see you', not even a link to the profile. The step list and the card also say the same thing twice ('Step 1 of 5' and '0 of 5 steps complete'). Setup therefore feels like filing paperwork with Eleva instead of opening a practice. The repo already prototyped the answer in PoC O8 Live Preview (_context/PoCs/expert-onboarding/walkthroughs/onboarding-live-preview/) and classic PoC B.
findings.recommendation: Replace the static left column with a live profile card that fills in as she answers: photo or initials, name, profession, languages, how she sees members, first service with price, and a 'Verified by Ordem' slot shown as pending. Empty parts show soft placeholders, so a new expert with no photo still looks deliberate. On mobile, put a 'Preview' button in the header that opens the card as a sheet. Show a full preview before she sends for review.

findings.title: The payouts step does not say Stripe, what she will need, or when she gets paid
findings.detail: The whole step is two sentences and a button in an otherwise empty card: 'Complete Payments setup to receive payouts. This stays on this page — no redirects.' and 'Start Payments setup'. It talks about how the page is built, not about her money. It never names Stripe, although the next thing she sees is a Stripe form asking for identity and bank details. It does not say what to have ready (ID document, IBAN), how long it takes, when earnings reach her bank, or what Eleva keeps. The subtitle says 'You can finish this later' but the capture shows no way to do that before starting. Asking for a bank account with this little context is where cautious professionals stop. The repo's PoC S7 (_context/PoCs/expert-onboarding/walkthroughs/setup-stripe-connect/) covers the hand-off mechanics; the missing piece is the framing.
findings.recommendation: Retitle 'Get paid for your sessions'. Before the Stripe form, show a short frame: who (Eleva sends your earnings through Stripe, the payments company; your bank details go to Stripe, not to Eleva staff), what you need (an identity document and your IBAN, about five minutes), when (how soon after a session money arrives) and what Eleva keeps, stated as a plain number. Two buttons: 'Set up payouts' and 'Do this later'. If she skips, the checklist says 'Add your bank account to receive earnings' and members can still be shown the profile once verified, or not, by product rule; say which.

findings.title: The invoicing step leads with two greyed-out options and ends on a legal warning
findings.detail: Two of three cards are disabled: TOConline ('Automatic invoice issuance is not active yet') and Moloni ('Coming soon'), each with a faded button. The only working choice is 'Manual invoicing', which asks her to tick 'I understand and accept this invoicing obligation' and press a button labelled 'Acknowledge manual invoicing'. The step reads as unfinished product followed by a liability notice, and it tells the expert what Eleva does not do, which the voice rules forbid. The chips 'PT' and 'PT, ES, BR' are unexplained. No Mobbin reference shows an invoicing-method choice like this one; the closest lesson is Fresha's fees card, which states terms as short, positive facts in one card.
findings.recommendation: Show only what works today. One card: 'You issue your own invoices', one sentence on why (each member needs a certified invoice for a session paid through Eleva, from your own invoicing software), the tax number field moved here from step 1, the checkbox, and a normal 'Continue' button. Remove the disabled provider cards until a provider is live; add them back as real choices then. Drop the country chips or write them out ('Available in Portugal, Spain and Brazil').

findings.title: Two step counters back to back: 'Step 2 of 2' with a full bar, then 'Step 1 of 5'
findings.detail: Naming the workspace is labelled 'Step 2 of 2' and its progress bar is already 100% full before she has typed anything. She presses 'Create workspace' expecting to be done and lands on 'Step 1 of 5' with '0 of 5 steps complete'. The finish line moved. An expert should always know how far along she is; here the product tells her twice, differently.
findings.recommendation: Make it one journey with one progress indicator from the type choice to 'send for review'. The practice name becomes an early step of the same flow (or is prefilled and editable inside 'About you'), and the bar only fills for work done. Airbnb's three chapters with a segmented bar and Wise's named stepper, visible from the account-type screen onward, are the models.

findings.title: The workspace type picker speaks software, not care
findings.detail: 'Create a workspace. Choose the type of workspace you want to create.' is a generic SaaS screen. It introduces a third word (workspace) next to Space and practice, gives the three cards equal weight though nearly everyone here is a solo expert, needs two taps (select, then a small 'Continue' that sits below the fold on mobile), and says nothing about what each path involves or whether the choice can be changed. The descriptions are organisational ('Manage multiple experts under one organization') rather than about the person choosing. The repo holds two good forks already: Time2book (Client vs Business) and Hims category cards under _context/mobbin/Apps/web/onboarding/.
findings.recommendation: Ask a human question: 'How will you offer care on Eleva?' Cards in her words: 'On my own' (I see members under my own name), 'With a team or clinic' (several experts, one practice), 'I teach courses'. Tap a card to continue; no separate button. Mark 'On my own' as the common choice, and add one line of reassurance: 'You can add another later.' Use 'practice' for the expert's place and keep 'Space' for the personal one.

findings.title: 'Workspace name' gives no help with what to type
findings.detail: One empty field with the placeholder 'My workspace' and the helper 'This is how your workspace will appear in Eleva.' A solo midwife does not know whether to type her own name, a brand, or anything at all, or whether members will see it. The field is not prefilled even though Eleva already has her name, and the page is otherwise blank. The repo's Fresha flow handles the same moment well: 'What's your business name? This is the brand name your clients will see. Your billing and legal name can be added later.' Attio (same folder) previews the workspace handle as you type.
findings.recommendation: Prefill with her name ('Marta Silva'), label it 'Practice name', and say who sees it: 'Members see this on your profile. Most experts use their own name.' Show the public link forming underneath (eleva.care/marta-silva) and the profile card from ONB-05 beside it. Reassure that the invoicing name is separate and comes later.

findings.title: The licence check has no step of its own, no example and no timeline
findings.detail: Professional body, licence number and ERS registration number are the fields that decide whether she can practise on Eleva, yet they sit two-thirds down a long form with the explanation collapsed behind 'Why we ask for this'. There is no picture or hint of where the cédula number is found beyond one line, no word on who can see these numbers, and no estimate of how long verification takes, on this step or the last. After she sends, the captures show no status. No Mobbin screen for a clinician licence was found; the references are identity and business-proof checks from other domains, used for structure.
findings.recommendation: Give the licence its own step, 'Your licence'. Open with three short lines in the Etsy pattern: what Eleva checks (your registration with your Ordem), who sees it (members see 'Verified'; the number stays private, or is shown, by product rule), and how long it takes. Add a 'Where do I find this?' example per Ordem. After sending, show a three-stage tracker on Today (Sent, In review, Verified) with the expected wait and 'We'll email you', as Airwallex does.

findings.title: The finish step has no reward, and its four next-step cards are not links
findings.detail: The teal banner is the best moment in the flow, but the four cards under it ('Create your first service and set its price', 'Set the weekly hours members can book', 'Connect Google or Microsoft calendars', 'Polish your public profile with a photo and bio') look tappable and are plain text (no links in step-finish.tsx). The things that make a practice bookable are listed as optional reading, with no order, no time estimates and no state. There is no preview of the profile she is sending, no celebration after sending, and the progress card still reads '0 of 5'. A first-week checklist does not exist yet; the repo's PoC S2 Dashboard Quest, S4 Todo Board and S9 Publish Checklist explore it, as does the Shopify setup guide in _context/mobbin/Apps/web/setting up/Shopify Account Setup/.
findings.recommendation: End setup with 'Review and send': the profile preview, then one button. Follow with a short success screen ('Your practice is in review') showing the tracker from ONB-11. Then make Today the checklist home until the practice is live: 'Welcome, Marta. Members can book you once your licence is verified. Here is how to prepare', with the four tasks as real links that tick off, each with a time estimate, plus 'Share your profile link' once verified. Tie the bar to an outcome ('Complete your profile to appear in search'), not to a count.

findings.title: On mobile the header block and unlabelled step dots push the question off the first screen
findings.detail: On a 390 px screen the eyebrow, 'Set up your practice', the subtitle, the progress card and a row of five numbered circles take the first 380 px on every step, so the actual question starts below the fold each time. The circles carry no labels, so the expert cannot tell what steps 3 to 5 are. Buttons are small left-aligned pills at the end of long scrolls ('Save and continue', 'Start Payments setup'), not thumb-width, and the card-inside-card layout on the invoicing step leaves about 250 px of usable text width.
findings.recommendation: Mobile layout: a thin segmented bar under the header with 'Step 2 of 6 · Your licence', the question as the page heading, one decision per screen, and a full-width 'Continue' fixed to the bottom with Back at top left. Show the title block once, on a welcome screen, not on every step. Drop nested cards on small screens.

findings.title: Nothing tells her what setup involves before it starts
findings.detail: Between choosing 'Expert' and the first tax field there is no screen that says how long setup takes, what to have at hand (cédula number, IBAN, tax number), what Eleva keeps from each session, or when members can start booking. The expert learns each requirement only by running into it, which is how the licence and bank steps turn into drop-off points. Airbnb spends one screen on 'It's easy to get started' with three numbered chapters; Whatnot lists fees and rules under 'Here's what to know before you get started'; Fresha shows an 'Overview of fees' card first.
findings.recommendation: Add one welcome screen after the type choice: 'Open your practice on Eleva' with three chapters (About you, Your licence, Getting paid), 'about 10 minutes', a 'Have these ready' line, the fee stated plainly, and 'You can save and come back at any time'. Each chapter then opens with a one-line intro of why it is asked.

findings.title: Small wording slips that make the wizard feel unedited
findings.detail: The primary button is 'Save and continue' on step 1 and 'Save & continue' on step 2. Step 1 is titled 'Your details' but holds a tax number and meeting modes. 'Start Payments setup' capitalises Payments as if it were a product name. 'Pick all that apply. Online is used if you leave this empty.' explains a system default instead of asking. 'Clinical modes' and 'non-clinical only' are internal terms. No Mobbin reference is needed for these; they are editing fixes.
findings.recommendation: One button label everywhere ('Continue'; saving is implied and can be confirmed with a quiet 'Saved'). Name each step after its question. Write for the expert: 'How do you see members?', 'Get paid for your sessions'. Replace 'clinical modes' with the plain thing it means, or remove it with the field (ONB-04).

references.pattern: Supply-side entry in the guest header, a three-chapter overview, chapter intros and one question per screen
references.why: 01a: the guest home keeps 'Become a host' in the header next to the avatar, so the supply path is always one click away. 01b: 'It's easy to get started on Airbnb' lists three numbered chapters with one line each before any question is asked. 01c: each chapter opens with 'Step 1', a title, two sentences on what will be asked, and a bar split into three segments; 'Questions?' and 'Save & exit' sit top right and there is no site navigation. 01d: a single question with three large options and nothing else on the page.
references.apply: Put 'Offer care on Eleva' in the member Space chrome. Add a welcome overview with three chapters. Run setup full screen with Save and exit, a help link and segmented progress. One question per screen.
references.query: marketplace host onboarding creating a first listing

references.pattern: Two-sided role choice at the door, and a seller prompt on the buyer home
references.why: 02a: the first screen offers two cards over a photo, 'Find a Service' (I'm looking for talented people to work with) and 'Selling services' (I'd like to offer my services); one tap chooses. 02b: someone who chose selling still lands on the buyer home, but a green 'Set up your seller profile' banner with 'Learn How' sits at the top so the path is never lost. A marketplace for freelance work, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Ask or carry the role before the first landing, write the options in the person's own words, and keep a visible 'finish setting up your practice' banner on the member Space for anyone who started as an expert.

references.pattern: Account type choice with a named stepper and 'you can add another later'
references.why: The question is conversational ('What kind of account would you like to open today?'), the two cards are large with an illustration and one line each, the line under the heading says 'You can add another account later on, too', and a stepper across the top (Account type, Country, 2FA, Password) already shows the whole journey. A finance product, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Rewrite the type picker as a question, make the cards tap-to-continue, add the reassurance line, and show the same progress indicator that the rest of setup uses.
references.query: marketplace sign up screen choosing an account type

references.pattern: One question on the left, the profile card it builds on the right
references.why: The left half holds a single prompt ('Tell us about yourself.') with one text box, Back and Continue. The right half shows the person's card (photo, name, role) that the answers feed. Nothing else is on the page. An HR onboarding tool, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Use this split for 'About you', 'How you see members' and 'Your first service': the question on one side, the Eleva profile card filling in on the other. On mobile the card becomes a Preview sheet.
references.query: profile setup onboarding step with a live preview of the public profile

references.pattern: Payout step framed as 'How you'll get paid', placed after the shop exists
references.why: The stepper names every stage in the seller's words (Shop preferences, Name your shop, How you'll get paid, Share your billing info, Your shop security), with money after the shop. The step is titled 'How you'll get paid' with a 'Protected' tag and a row of accepted payment logos, a green confirmation that the previous part was saved, plain sentences about reserves for new shops, and a 'Heads up' on what cannot be changed later.
references.apply: Title the Stripe step by its benefit, place it after the profile and licence, name the payment partner, confirm what was just saved, and state the rules that matter (timing, fees) before the form.
references.query: marketplace seller setting up payouts to a bank account

references.pattern: Verification step that explains why, who does it and what comes next
references.why: The heading promises 'just a few steps'. One paragraph gives the reason (protect the marketplace, keep the community safe) and names the partner that does the check. Three rows show what will happen in order, ending with 'Finish setting up your shop: once your identity is verified, you'll be able to continue'. The data already on file is shown with an edit control.
references.apply: Open 'Your licence' the same way: why Eleva checks, that it checks with the Ordem, three rows for what happens (enter your number, we check the register, members see Verified), and what she can do while she waits.
references.query: healthcare provider onboarding professional licence verification screen

references.pattern: Proof-of-eligibility step written as a conversation, with options explained and an example
references.why: 'Step 2 of 3. Next, we need some proof of business ownership. What documents do you have on hand?' Each option has a sentence saying what the document is and who issues it, the chosen one opens an upload area with what must be visible and a 'See example' link, and a warm product photo fills the other half so the step does not feel like a form. A wholesale marketplace, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Ask for the licence as a question ('Which Ordem are you registered with?'), explain each number in a line, add 'See where to find it', and keep the profile card or a calm image beside it.
references.query: healthcare provider onboarding professional licence verification screen

references.pattern: Submitted-for-review screen with a three-stage tracker and a stated wait
references.why: 'Thank you for submitting your application' sits over a tracker (Sign up: Completed, Verification: In review, Activation: Pending). A card says 'We are reviewing your details' and that the team expects to get back 'within 1-3 business days', followed by 'Return to Dashboard' and things to explore meanwhile. A finance product, kept for its structure.
references.apply: After 'Send for review', show Sent, In review, Verified with the expected wait and 'We'll email you', then lead into the checklist of things to do while waiting. Repeat the tracker on Today.
references.query: marketplace provider application submitted and under review screen

references.pattern: Marketplace profile setup: fees first, preview before publishing, a shareable link at the end
references.why: 09a: the first step is 'Overview of fees', one card with three plain rows and a tag on each, in a full-screen layout with a thin progress bar and one 'Next step' button. 09b: 'You're almost done! Preview your profile and see how it would look' with 'Preview profile' and 'Publish' side by side. 09c: 'Your Fresha profile is ready!' with the booking link and copy control, three follow-up actions (tell your clients, QR code, import clients) and 'See your profile'. A beauty and wellness booking marketplace, the closest domain match found.
references.apply: State Eleva's fee plainly before setup. Let the expert preview her profile before sending it for review. When she is verified, give her the profile link to copy and two or three first actions.
references.query: marketplace host onboarding creating a first listing

references.pattern: The Today page as the post-setup checklist
references.why: After listing, the host's Today page says 'Welcome, Nabila! Guests can reserve your place 24 hours after you publish, here's how to prepare.' One card is marked 'Required to publish' with Start. Below, 'Your next steps' shows optional tasks as cards with an icon, a title and one line each (Instant Book, calendar, cancellation policy, house rules). The full host navigation is available.
references.apply: Once the required steps are sent, Today becomes the checklist home: a greeting that states when members can book, required items marked as such, and the same next steps Eleva already lists (first service, weekly hours, calendars, photo and bio) as real links.
references.query: booking software dashboard home with a setup checklist

references.pattern: Profile completion tied to an outcome
references.why: A 'Profile completion 14%' bar tagged 'High impact' sits over a panel that says 'Unlock discoverability by completing your profile. Once you're done, you'll start appearing in search results.' with one 'Complete profile' button. The percentage is given a reason. A freelance marketplace, kept for its structure.
references.apply: Replace '0 of 5 steps complete' with progress that names the reward: 'Finish your profile to appear in search' and 'Add your bank account to receive earnings'.
references.query: booking marketplace sign up page with a separate link for professionals

references.pattern: Mobile seller setup: benefits sheet, what to know, one question per screen, a first-week checklist
references.why: 12a: from the buyer app a sheet asks 'Interested in Selling?' with three benefit lines, 'FAQ' and 'Get Started'. 12b: 'Ready to earn? Here's what to know before you get started' lists the fee and the rules in five short rows before any form. 12c: one question per screen ('How big is your team?') with a line on why it is asked, a thin progress bar and a thumb-reach 'Next'. 12d: 'Get Ready to Go Live' is a celebration followed by an ordered checklist and a time-boxed incentive. A live-shopping marketplace, kept for its mobile structure.
references.apply: On mobile: a benefits sheet from the member Space, a what-to-know screen with Eleva's fee and requirements, one question per screen with a bottom button, and a finish screen that turns into an ordered first-week checklist.

references.pattern: A 'Verifying' pill and a secondary Edit button on the same card as the submitted details
references.why: While personal details are being verified, the card still shows what was sent, a 'Verifying' pill with an info icon, and a plain 'Edit' button beside it. Nothing about the waiting state takes the right to correct away.
references.apply: On the licence page's pending card, keep the summary of Ordem, cédula and ERS, and put a small outline 'Edit details' button next to it.
references.query: verification under review status screen with an edit details option

references.pattern: Per-item 'Verifying' tag with a pencil to correct it, plus a banner saying you can carry on
references.why: 'Verification in progress, you can continue…' sits above the list; the item under review has a 'Verifying' tag and a pencil button, the verified one only a view icon. Editing is offered exactly where verification is still open, not once it is done.
references.apply: Offer editing while pending, never once verified (verified stays support-only), and keep the 'meanwhile you can set up your services' line.
references.query: verification under review status screen with an edit details option

references.pattern: A waiting screen whose secondary action fixes the thing being waited on
references.why: 15a: 'Please verify your email' names the address and offers 'Update email' next to 'Resend email'. 15b: Stripe's 'Verify your email' says 'You can also change your email if you need to.' The fix for a typo lives on the waiting screen itself, as the quieter action.
references.apply: The correction is a secondary action on the pending card, with one line saying sending again restarts the check, so the expert knows the cost before she presses it.
references.query: verification under review status screen with an edit details option

judging_criteria: Can a person who signed up to offer care reach expert setup from her first screen without opening a menu? (06-expert-onboarding/01, 06-expert-onboarding/02)

Does setup run without dashboard navigation, with Save and exit, a help link and one progress indicator from the first question to 'send for review'? (06-expert-onboarding/01, 06-expert-onboarding/09)
Does every screen ask for one thing, with a line saying why it is asked, and a primary button within thumb reach on a 390 px screen? (06-expert-onboarding/01, 06-expert-onboarding/12)
Do the first three steps build the public profile (who she is, how she sees members, a first service), with tax, payouts and invoices after them? (06-expert-onboarding/01, 06-expert-onboarding/05)
Can she see her profile card update while she answers, and preview the full profile before sending it? (06-expert-onboarding/04, 06-expert-onboarding/09)

Before any bank or identity form, does the screen name Stripe, list what she needs, and say when and how much she is paid, with a way to do it later? (06-expert-onboarding/05, 06-expert-onboarding/12)

After she sends her licence, does she see a status with an expected wait, and a Today page whose next steps are real links tied to an outcome? (06-expert-onboarding/08, 06-expert-onboarding/10, 06-expert-onboarding/11)

While her licence is being checked, can she correct a typo from the status card in one step, and does the page say the check restarts? (06-expert-onboarding/13, 06-expert-onboarding/14, 06-expert-onboarding/15)
